This file is for doing data tidying. 

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

## Let's tidy some data!

```{r}
pulse_df = 
  haven::read_sas("data/public_pulse_data.sas7bdat") |> 
  janitor::clean_names()
```


Okay, let's tidy!

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pulse_tidy_df =
  pulse_df |> 
  pivot_longer(
    bdi_score_bl:bdi_score_12m,
    names_to = "visit",
    names_prefix = "bdi_score_",
    values_to = "bdi_score"
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    visit = replace(visit, visit == "bl", "00m")
  )
```

Just use once ..

```{r}
pulse_df = 
  haven::read_sas("data/public_pulse_data.sas7bdat") |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  pivot_longer(
    bdi_score_bl:bdi_score_12m,
    names_to = "visit",
    names_prefix = "bdi_score_",
    values_to = "bdi_score"
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    visit = replace(visit, visit == "bl", "00m")
  )
```


Let's practice!

Import the litters data; keep columns litter number and GD weights; and tidy.

```{r}
litters_df = 
  read_csv("data/FAS_litters.csv", na = c(".", "", "NA")) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  select(litter_number, gd0_weight, gd18_weight) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    gd0_weight:gd18_weight,
    names_to = "gd", 
    values_to = "weight"
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    gd = case_match(
      gd, 
      "gd0_weight"  ~ 0, 
      "gd18_weight" ~ 18, 
    )
  )
```
